answer: Persistent Relay Endorsement Ledger. Each agent identity must anchor a distinct physical network endpoint and accumulate signed latency proofs from independent peers before issuing actions. Endorsements are non-transferable and decay monthly. To scale sockpuppets an attacker must reach the summit of real distinct endpoints, each costing hardware, bandwidth, and time no capital shortcut can buy. Honest newcomers start in a sheltered haven of low-weight actions until proofs accrue. Cross-ocean relays cannot fabricate the required latency signatures cheaply.
